extracted.intended_audience: educators, educational theorists, and teachers (students of pedagogy)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for establishing, evaluating, and implementing aims in education (how aims should be formed, tested, and translated into methods). Useful for teachers, curriculum designers, and educational theorists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must be an outgrowth of existing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim set up must be an outgrowth of existing conditions. It must be based upon a consideration of what is already going on; upon the resources and difficulties of the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theories that assume ends lying outside activities (externally supplied aims) limit intelligence; ready-made aims imposed by authority leave only a mechanical choice of means. Good aims emerge from observation of present circumstances (examples: farmer, teacher).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim should be tentative and revisable (flexibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim as it first emerges is a mere tentative sketch. The act of striving to realize it tests its worth; acting upon it brings to light conditions which call for revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims must be capable of alteration to meet circumstances; they are experimental and grow as they are tested in action. By contrast, externally established ends are rigid and not corrected by experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must represent a freeing of activities (end-as-means)
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim must always represent a freeing of activities: the object is a mark or sign directing activity, and the doing with the thing (the activity) is the end, not the thing in isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid divorcing means from ends; every means is a temporary end and every end becomes a means. A legitimate aim makes activity significant at each stage rather than reducing it to drudgery (example: farmer fond of his work vs. farmer using animals merely as means).

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational aims must be founded on the individual's intrinsic activities and needs
rubrics_metrics.description: An educational aim must be founded upon the intrinsic activities and needs (including original instincts and acquired habits) of the given individual to be educated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not set adult-centered or uniform aims that ignore the specific powers, timing, and situations of learners. Use adult accomplishments only as context for understanding a child's activities, not as fixed aims imposed on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must be translatable into cooperative methods
rubrics_metrics.description: An aim must be capable of translation into a method of cooperating with the activities of those undergoing instruction; it must suggest the kind of environment needed to liberate and organize their capacities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless an aim lends itself to specific procedures that test, correct, and amplify it, it is worthless. Rigid externally given aims prevent ordinary judgment and attention to relevant details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid externally imposed aims from authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims received from superior authorities, textbooks, or prescribed courses limit the teacher's intelligence and lead teachers and pupils to accept aims without close observation or judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External imposition causes double/triple imposition on pupils and confuses them between natural aims and imposed aims; promotes mechanical, slavish instruction rather than democratic, reflective practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against overly general, abstract, or ultimate ends
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of ends alleged to be general and ultimate; while a general aim broadens outlook, if it is abstract and detached from context it becomes remote and turns teaching/learning into mere preparation for something else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truly general aims should broaden observation and suggest multiple starting places; a plurality of comprehensive aims can coexist and supplement one another. An aim is educative only if it is worthwhile in its immediate having.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim is the foresight of alternative consequences and a guide to observation/experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: An aim denotes foresight of the alternative consequences attendant upon acting in different ways and the use of that anticipation to direct observation and experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A true aim connects with present activities and stimulates intelligent decision-making; it is tested and refined through action rather than imposed as a fixed external end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural development should inform but not supply the end
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature (native structure, capacities, dispositions) supplies conditions and limits for education but does not itself furnish the ends of development; native activities are foundations, not goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rousseau's mistake is taking spontaneous native development as the end. Instead, adult-guided uses of native capacities organize and direct growth; do not leave development entirely to spontaneous processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make health and physical vigor an educational aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural development as an aim fixes attention upon the bodily organs and the need of health and vigor; make health an aim because normal development requires bodily vigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizing health as an aim should lead to changes in educational practice (e.g., more attention to physical conditions, schedules, and activities that support vigor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect physical mobility and bodily activity in education
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of following nature translates into regard for physical mobility: children are in motion and a sedentary life is injurious; bodily exercise contributes to mental development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design activities that allow exploration, handling materials, play and games; bodily exercise is a route to cognitive development rather than an obstacle to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and utilize individual differences and special bents
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of natural development implies regard for individual differences in temperament, capacities, and timing; education should prefer irregular, budding growth to artificial uniformity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe spontaneous sayings and doings, 'strike while the iron is hot' for early dawning powers, avoid stunting true gifts by forcing uniform exercises, and create environments that nurture varied developmental paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an environment that organizes and utilizes instincts
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural tendencies must be given an environment which organizes them and puts them to useful ends rather than being left to 'spontaneous development' alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adults should not simply accept children's impulses as ends; instead create contexts in which desirable tendencies remain active and lead other tendencies into useful directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social efficiency: positive utilization of native capacities for social ends
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of social efficiency emphasizes using native individual capacities in occupations and activities having social meaning, focusing on positive use rather than mere subordination to rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid approaches that subordinate individuals to class authority or that merely habituate them to control; seek to harness individual powers in socially constructive ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial competency as an educational aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should foster industrial competency — the ability to earn a livelihood and manage economic resources usefully rather than for display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not train for overly specific callings tied to current industry structures (they change rapidly); avoid perpetuating social inequities by assigning occupations based on parental wealth or status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic efficiency (good citizenship) as an educational aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Civic efficiency denotes capacities that make an individual a competent citizen: the ability to judge men and measures wisely and to take part in making as well as obeying laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret civic efficiency broadly (so as not to exclude scientific or theoretical pursuits); ultimately it means the capacity to share in the give-and-take of social experience.
